---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Persistent Accrual NetExternalFinance
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with persistently high accrual earnings that are simultaneously raising net external capital will underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The three-period average focuses on sustained accounting-quality weakness rather than a noisy one-year accrual spike. Pairing that persistence with net equity and debt issuance tests whether outside financing is most bearish when reported earnings have repeatedly exceeded cash flow.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: EquityFunded Receivables Inventory Build
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms issuing net equity while receivables and inventories are consuming cash will earn lower future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The accrual leg is sign-corrected so that high values represent receivable and inventory increases, not liquidation. Equity issuance during this operating build may indicate that reported growth is not converting into cash and is being supported by external shareholders.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Rollover Accrual Fragility
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(dltt, 1)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: High-accrual firms shifting toward current debt relative to long-term debt will underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This avoids the mechanical conflict between working-capital accruals and short-term debt by using the earnings-minus-cash-flow accrual gap rather than Δwcap. A rising current-debt share alongside weak cash conversion suggests refinancing pressure and less room to absorb accrual reversals.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: DebtFunded Payout Accrual Mask
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high accrual income that borrow while making payouts will subsequently underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Payouts can be favorable when supported by cash generation, but debt-funded payouts are more suspect when earnings quality is weak. The three-way interaction targets financial engineering: reported profits, external borrowing, and capital distributions occurring together.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: AccrualPeak ShareDiluter
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)), RANK(GROWTH(csho, 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Share dilution is especially bearish when the firm’s accrual gap is high relative to its own recent history.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This repairs the prior binary-gate issue by keeping both legs continuous and rankable. A shorter three-period own-history rank captures issuance timed to unusually aggressive accounting without the coverage loss and tail contamination of a long-window indicator.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: CashBacked Debt Retirement
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ib), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with cash earnings exceeding accounting earnings and net debt retirement will earn higher future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Strong cash conversion indicates conservative accounting or earnings backed by real cash flow. When that cash quality is paired with debt reduction rather than new borrowing, it signals balance-sheet repair and lower financing pressure.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

RATIONALE: This is essentially the sign-mirrored twin of the archived "Clean Accrual Net Capital Return" (MA3 accrual gap × net financing/payout), differing only by dropping dvc and flipping both legs, so it re-tests an already-evaluated interaction rather than adding new information.

---CRITIQUE EquityFunded Receivables Inventory Build---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The recch/invch sign correction is handled correctly and the equity-issuance pairing is a defensible variant on the failed debt-funded version, but it remains a straightforward product of two well-known anomalies (working-capital accruals and net share issuance) with limited incremental novelty.

---CRITIQUE Rollover Accrual Fragility---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Combining the earnings-minus-cash accrual gap with a genuine debt-maturity-shift leg (Δdlc − Δdltt) is economically coherent, internally consistent in sign, and distinct from both the archived debt-issuance variants and standard published accrual/issuance anomalies.

---CRITIQUE DebtFunded Payout Accrual Mask---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The expected negative sign conflicts with the payout leg, whose natural direction (buyback/dividend yield, and the archived positive-alpha payout composite) is positive, and the triple rank product neither identifies that payouts are actually debt-funded nor survives the dilution/noise of three multiplied ranks.

---CRITIQUE AccrualPeak ShareDiluter---
VERDICT: flag

RATIONALE: This is a cosmetic re-specification of the archived "Continuous Dilution Accrual Deterioration" (csho growth × accrual-gap change) with DELTA swapped for a 3-observation TS_RANK that can take only a handful of coarse values, so it is unlikely to fix the earlier weak result.

---CRITIQUE CashBacked Debt Retirement---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Low accruals × net debt retirement is nearly the archived "Clean Accrual Net Capital Return" with the MA(3) smoothing and equity/dividend payout terms stripped out, making it a weaker restatement of an already-tested and already-successful signal rather than a new mechanism.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: DebtAdjusted CurrentAccrual Issuer
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1))), ADD(DELTA(lct, 1), dp)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high debt-adjusted current accruals while raising net external capital will underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This uses a balance-sheet accrual construction that explicitly adds back current debt changes, avoiding the mechanical short-debt versus working-capital conflict. The financing leg captures net external capital raising, so the signal targets firms whose noncash operating accrual buildup is being supported by outside capital rather than internal cash generation.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: DebtFunded Payout CashShortfall
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), RANK(MIN(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at), SUB(RATIO(ADD(prstkc, dvc), at), RATIO(oancf, at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: High-accrual firms that borrow while payouts exceed internally generated operating cash flow will earn lower future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The financing leg is high only when net debt issuance and a payout-versus-cash-flow shortfall are both elevated, directly identifying the debt-funded payout mechanism. This avoids treating payouts as mechanically bearish; payouts become negative only when paired with weak cash conversion and external borrowing.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: OperatingLiability EquityIssuer Stress
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(apalch, txach), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms issuing net equity while stretching operating liabilities through payables and tax accruals will underperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Increases in payables and tax accruals can temporarily preserve cash by delaying payments to suppliers or tax authorities. When a firm is still issuing equity despite this operating-liability financing, it suggests deeper balance-sheet pressure rather than healthy growth financing.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: AccrualRepair Deleveraging
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(lt, at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with improving accrual quality and declining leverage will earn higher subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: A falling earnings-minus-cash-flow accrual gap indicates improving cash backing of reported earnings. When that improvement coincides with lower liabilities relative to assets, the accounting-quality repair is reinforced by balance-sheet repair rather than isolated accrual mean reversion.
